subject: Clarify obligations: incident timeline, affected dataflows, and subprocessor transfers
messages:
From: Jordan Miles <security@finclave.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@finclave.com
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Possible data export observed — please confirm DPA notification window

Alex —

We found an anomalous export from our account (finclave-prod) yesterday evening that looks like a partial user record dump. We're still triaging but wanted to alert you immediately since the contract references a 72-hour cooperative evidence handover and a 72–120 hour potential notification window depending on scope.

Can you confirm whether this meets Redwood's incident notification threshold and who on your side will be the point of contact for evidence transfer and subprocessor mapping? Also: are any subprocessors involved in the affected dataflow that would trigger cross-border transfers?

I've attached a short telemetry excerpt (redacted) and an initial timestamped event list. Happy to jump on a call if useful.

Thanks,
Jordan Miles
Head of Security
Finclave, Inc.
Attachment: telemetry_excerpt-20270702.txt
From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Miles <security@finclave.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Possible data export observed — please confirm DPA notification window

Jordan —

Thank you for flagging and for the excerpt — that helps. Short answers up front: we treat confirmed unauthorized exfiltration as a Notifiable Incident under our DPA; we will cooperate on evidence handover and notification timing per the contract.

Next steps I propose:
- I will triage with Security (Ben copied) to confirm scope within the next 6 hours.
- Kimberly (Privacy counsel) will review contract triggers and advise on whether expedited customer notification is required.
- Please preserve any logs you have and confirm the time range for the events in your excerpt. If you can provide a fuller packet (S3 access logs, export job id) that will speed triage.

Can you confirm the number of affected accounts and whether the payload included PII or machine-generated embeddings? That will influence the notification timing and whether cross-border data subjects are implicated.

We can set up a secure file share for evidence transfer — sharing a Drive folder link now.

Regards,
Alex Martinez
Security Partner Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachment: forensic_request-form.pdf
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Miles <security@finclave.com>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Possible data export observed — please confirm DPA notification window

Jordan / Alex —

Appreciate the early notice. Per our DPA (Section 7: Incident Response and Notification), obligations depend on scope and whether Redwood processed customer personal data in an identifiable form that was exported. A few clarifying asks so I can map contractual triggers to operational steps: 

1) Data scope: a minimally sufficient sample of the payload will let us determine categories (PII, account identifiers, embeddings). Please mark any redactions but keep structural fields intact.
2) Subprocessors: attach a list or confirm if the export came from a managed storage service we operate versus a customer-managed bucket. If a Redwood subprocessor (e.g., third-party backup/ingest), we will need to notify and coordinate their forensic output as part of the 72h evidence handover.
3) Cross-border: indicate origin IPs / region flags for the export job. If EU/UK data subjects are implicated, notification timing and DPA obligations shift.

Operational commitments we can make now: 
- Acknowledgement within 24 hours of any confirmed Notifiable Incident.
- Forensic intake (secure upload + checklist) within 72 hours once scope is confirmed.
- We will produce a subprocessor mapping and export manifest within 5 business days, or sooner if evidence suggests immediate cross-border transfer.

Please upload the fuller packet to the Drive link Alex provided or reply with S3 pre-signed links. Once we have the artifacts, Ben will coordinate the forensic timeline and I will coordinate communications/legal decisions.

Kimberly Park
Senior Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Miles <security@finclave.com>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 14:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Possible data export observed — please confirm DPA notification window

Jordan —

We triaged the telemetry you sent and matched it to an export job id. At a high level:
- Preliminary scope: export appears to contain user profile fields + hashed identifiers (no obvious full SSNs in the sample). We will treat this as potentially Notifiable until full payload validated.
- Subprocessors: preliminary checks show the job traversed our ingestion queue and a third-party backup service (StorageCo) for short-term staging — we are engaging them now.

Proposed immediate cooperation plan: 
1) Acknowledgement email (this thread) — complete.
2) Secure intake: please upload the full packet to the Drive folder (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-finclave-incident) or send pre-signed S3 links. We will ingest into our forensic environment within 24h of receiving.
3) Evidence handover timeline: we commit to producing our export manifest and initial forensic snapshot within 72h of your packet receipt. If cross-border transfers are identified, we will prioritize a subprocessor mapping within that 72h window and escalate to Kimberly for notification decisions.
4) Call: proposing a 30-minute bridge at 16:00 PT today to align on handover format and roles.

If that plan looks good, confirm and upload the packet. We will keep a running shared timeline in the Drive folder (link above).

Ben Carter
Security Incident Response Lead, Redwood Inference
